channel.title: The U-Curve Brain
channel.description: A macro-autonomous cognitive filter. Optimizing for agency, perspective, and resilience.

item.title: (Audio) Angus Buchan on the nature of peacemaking
item.description:
Source: Thought For Today



Angus Buchan discusses the concept of peacemaking from a Christian perspective, drawing from Matthew 5:9. He differentiates between peace-lovers and peace-makers, emphasizing the active role and humility involved in creating peace.

item.title: (Research) Treatments improve for a previously fatal protein-related disease
item.description:
Source: Works in Progress RSS Feed

This article discusses a disease, once considered a death sentence, which is now increasingly treatable. It explores advancements in medical understanding and treatment protocols for a protein-related condition. Awareness of medical breakthroughs can inform professionals in health-related fields or those supporting innovation.

item.title: (Research) Restorative justice: Joan Scourfield and her son's killer share a stage
item.description:
Source: Positive News

Through a restorative justice program, Joan Scourfield shares a stage with the man convicted of killing her son. They discuss forgiveness publicly, demonstrating the process's capacity for healing. Understanding restorative justice models can offer new perspectives on conflict resolution for professionals.

item.title: (Video) Copenhagen Atomics develops thorium nuclear reactor technology
item.description:
Source: minutephysics



This video explores the development of thorium nuclear reactors and Copenhagen Atomics' progress towards commercializing thorium energy. It discusses the potential benefits of this alternative nuclear technology.

item.title: (Audio) Megan Leslie's podcast features people protecting nature
item.description:
Source: Antica Productions, WWF-Canada



WWF-Canada CEO Megan Leslie interviews individuals working to protect nature. The podcast showcases positive efforts and demonstrates that conservation change is actively happening, fostering hope for the environment.

System Note: While concerns for nature are valid, this podcast highlights ongoing efforts by many individuals and organizations, showing agency and tangible progress in conservation.

item.title: (Audio) A children's podcast explores diverse flowers
item.description:
Source: Lenore Elizabeth Mulets



This podcast volume features stories, poems, and facts about a diverse array of flowers, designed for children. It explores unique flora across thirteen parts, fostering engagement with the natural world.

item.title: (Audio) Mary Garcia's podcast explores nature through stories, poetry, and facts
item.description:
Source: Mary Garcia / SmartSeeds



Mary Garcia's podcast, 'Wild & Wonder,' blends fiction, poetry, and nature facts for children and adults. It explores changing seasons, language, and wildlife through stories, sounds, and reflection, fostering curiosity about the natural world.

item.title: (Video) Dr. Azra Raza advocates a patient-centered approach in cancer treatment
item.description:
Source: The New York Academy of Sciences



Dr. Azra Raza, a leading cancer physician and scientist, discusses her advocacy for a patient-centered approach in oncology. She shares perspectives from her personal and professional experience treating cancer patients.

item.title: (Video) Maya Higa's virtual wildlife sanctuary engages new conservationists
item.description:
Source: TED



Creator Maya Higa uses a virtual education center and the internet to engage and build the next generation of conservationists. Her work provides accessible ways for people to connect with wildlife.

item.title: (Video) Dark Matter: Unexpected Link with Lord Kelvin
item.description:
Source: Sixty Symbols



Professor Ed Copeland discusses the properties of dark matter, exploring its mysteries and an unexpected connection to the work of Lord Kelvin. The discussion provides insights into theoretical physics.

item.title: (Research) George Schaller's conservation research saved species
item.description:
Source: Undark Magazine



A book reviews George Schaller's extensive career in conservation biology. His pioneering research established the field and is credited with saving many species from extinction. The book documents his triumphs and challenges.

item.title: (Adage) Youth is wasted on the young (Use your present perspective to question fear-driven narratives now.)
Dedicated Minds Continually Remaking a Better World
item.description:
(Today) Progress unfolds through human ingenuity and compassionate action. Every breakthrough, every connection, shows our power to build a better world.

(Pattern) It's the persistent application of intellect and compassion, across all domains, to actively improve conditions and understanding.

(Reminder) Define the true scale of every challenge; that discernment is your fortress against manufactured anxieties.
